diagnostic_evidence.quote: For low-dimensional cases ($d=1, 2, 8$),  both the DBR and DBDP1 methods demonstrate satisfactory performance, achieving relative errors generally below $7\%$ across different $N$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims consistent outperformance and robust accuracy. The tables do not support this: for Example 2 at d=8 the listed DBDP1 relative errors and mean absolute errors are better than DBR for all shown N; the text itself says there is no decisive low-dimensional advantage. At d=20 the small DBR "Rel.err." is only the error of the 10-run sample mean, while the mean absolute error is 0.366364 with standard deviation 0.446021 against true value 0.259041, and for N=90,100 DBDP1 has smaller mean absolute error and standard deviation. Thus the evidence does not establish consistent outperformance or per-run relative errors under 9.7%.

failure_location.quote: Numerical results demonstrate that the DBR scheme consistently outperforms the DBDP1 method

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the numerical claims: drop "consistently", state explicitly that the reported relative error is the bias of the 10-run mean, and discuss the mean absolute error and standard deviation before claiming robustness.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical superiority/robustness claims in the abstract and introduction are materially overstated; the formal theorems are not directly affected.
issues.title: Abstract overclaims consistent numerical superiority and per-run robustness
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of numerical prose and metric interpretation; no theorem or algorithm guarantee depends on it, and a narrower high-dimensional claim remains supported by the defined relative-error column.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof equates the residual against the actual bootstrapped training label S_{y,i} with R_{i,2}^y. But R_{i,2}^y is defined using the exact discrete BSDE quantities Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m,k} and f(t_i,X_i^{\pi,m},Y_i^{\pi,m},Z_i^{\pi,m}), whereas S_{y,i} uses the previously trained network at i+1 and the current y-network iterate inside f. These are different random variables, and the analogous z equality has the same mismatch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the residuals to be the actual training-label residuals, or prove a rigorous estimate relating exact-BSDE labels to the bootstrapped labels at every backward step before inserting them into the Gronwall argument.
issues.overall_effect: The residual terms controlled in Theorem ae-DMCE are not the residuals minimized by the stated DBR losses, so the error representation used for Gronwall and later convergence is unreliable.
issues.title: Training-label residual is falsely identified with an exact-BSDE residual
issues.why_classification: The proof architecture can remain, but the residual definitions and at least one consistency estimate must be changed; this is more than a local typo yet does not by itself force abandonment of the error-bound framework.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding estimate bounds E|S_{y,i}-U_{t_i}^m|^2 by C(1+h) plus residual terms. After Young's inequality this produces an additional C(1+h) in E|Y_i-U_{t_i}^m|^2, but the displayed bound for E|Y_i-U_{t_i}^m|^2 keeps only residual terms. Because the earlier Gronwall estimate multiplies this quantity by 1/h and sums over N=Theta(1/h), retaining the omitted constant gives a Theta(h^{-2}) contribution, not the stated bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: A repair must prove the missing O(h) control of the centered bootstrapped label/conditional variance (with specified Monte Carlo sizes and any needed extra regularity) or else change the error bound; no such estimate is presently supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The main upper error bound is not proved as stated; the later half-order convergence theorem inherits the gap.
issues.title: An O(1) term is dropped before the 1/h Gronwall sum
issues.why_classification: Keeping the term that the proof actually derives destroys the asserted estimate, and obtaining the needed O(h) bound requires a new nontrivial conditional-variance/Monte Carlo argument rather than a local correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is verified with $R = O(N^{\frac{3}{2}}), \varepsilon = O(N^{-3}), K= O(N^{3})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The two Hölder exponents are 1/q and (2q-1)/q, whose sum is 2 rather than 1; for an indicator event of probability p this would falsely give p <= C p^{(2q-1)/q}. A correct estimate puts the indicator to power (q-1)/q and, with a 2q-moment Markov bound, yields tail decay O(R^{-2(q-1)})=O(R^{-delta}), not the displayed O(R^{-2}) unless a fourth-moment choice delta=2 is separately justified. Hence the later choice R=O(N^{3/2}), epsilon=O(N^{-3}) is unsupported for the stated arbitrary delta>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the Hölder and Markov exponents and either explicitly use a fourth moment (which must be stated or justified) to keep R=O(N^{3/2}), epsilon=O(N^{-3}), or recompute R, epsilon and the network size for the actual delta.
issues.overall_effect: The compact-domain approximation/tail balance and the resulting GroupSort network size are not established for the stated moment assumption.
issues.title: Invalid Hölder/Markov tail estimate in the convergence proof
issues.why_classification: The defect is a real invalid estimate, but it is contained in the tail step: a corrected moment/tail choice preserves the half-order conclusion, while the general-delta statement would need a restated complexity bound.

issues.failure_explanation: Equations (Deep-NN-E-r-7) and (Deep-NN-E-r-8) bound the population approximation infimum over a GroupSort class. Theorem ae-DMCE requires bounds for residuals of the empirical SGD minimizer computed from M sampled paths and K_i Monte Carlo labels, and also for the Monte Carlo residuals R_{i,1}^y,R_{i,1}^z. No finite-sample estimation error, SGD optimization error, or Monte Carlo rate in K_i is proved; writing K=O(N^3) in the parameter balance does not itself estimate those residuals.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a rigorous estimation/optimization analysis linking the empirical SGD minimizer to the best GroupSort approximant and prove the required R_{i,1}/R_{i,2} rates under explicit M and K_i; otherwise weaken the theorem to an ideal-approximator statement.
issues.overall_effect: The proved statement supports, at most, existence of ideal networks with small population error; it does not establish half-order convergence of the implementable trained DBR output.
issues.title: Best-approximation bounds are used as if they controlled the empirical SGD/Monte Carlo scheme
issues.why_classification: This changes the guarantee type from convergence of the actual algorithm to existence of a good population approximant unless substantial new statistical/optimization arguments are added.

issues.failure_explanation: In the discrete reflected BSDE, the continuation value and Z_i are computed from the already reflected next value Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m}=max{\bar Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m},g(X_{i+1}^{\pi,m})}. The RDBR construction applies the maximum only to the output at time i, while the labels/auxiliary quantities use the unreflected network NN_{y,i+1} at time i+1. When the constraint is active at i+1, the regression target is the wrong random variable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the reflected next value \widehat{\mathcal Y}_{i+1}=max{\widehat{NN}_{y,i+1},g(X_{i+1}^{\pi,m})} in S_{y,i}, S_{z,i}, \bar{\mathcal U}_{t_i}^m, \widehat{\mathcal V}_{t_i}^m and in the corresponding residuals, then propagate this change through the error proof.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the RDBR scheme does not implement the reflected Euler scheme on active-constraint states, so its variational-inequality guarantee and Theorem ae-DMCE-R are unreliable.
issues.title: RDBR recursion omits the reflection in the next-time regression target
issues.why_classification: The correction is the standard reflected-scheme modification, but it changes the construction and the proof rather than being a single forced symbol; a comparable RDBR method should survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The error estimate for the $Z$-component can be derived using the same arguments as in Steps 3 and 4 of the proof of Theorem \ref{ae-DMCE}; thus, the details are omitted here.
with $\varepsilon(h) = O(h^{1/2})$ under Assumption \ref{ass-1}, and $\varepsilon(h) = O(h)$ under  Assumption \ref{ass-2};

issues.failure_explanation: Combining max_i E|Y_i^{\pi,m}-\widehat{Y}_i|^2 with max_i E|Y_{t_i}-Y_i^{\pi,m}|^2=epsilon(h) must add a C epsilon(h) term; the displayed Y conclusion omits it and would falsely imply zero time-discretization error when the residuals vanish. In addition, the Z-component is only asserted by analogy even though the reflected-BSDE estimate quoted in the proof gives the Z time-discretization part as O(h^{1/2}); no argument is supplied for the claimed O(h) combined rate under Assumption ass-2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the C epsilon(h) term for Y and either prove the required reflected Z estimate, including any first-order improvement under Assumption ass-2, or weaken the combined bound to the supported O(h^{1/2}).
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not establish the stated RDBR error bound; in particular the first-order claim for the combined Y and Z error under Assumption ass-2 is unsupported.
issues.title: RDBR error proof drops the discretization error and leaves the Z rate unproved
issues.why_classification: Adding the omitted epsilon(h) is local, but the missing reflected-Z argument is nontrivial; a comparable half-order variational-inequality bound remains while the extra first-order claim is not established.
